(2)  Such new advances shall bear interest at prevailing
market-related rates as determined by the Central Bank.
(3)  Such new advances shall not be made to refinance
the outstanding credit of the Central Bank to the Government
on the appointed date.
(4)  The provisions of subsections (1), (2) and (3) of this
section shall be effective until such time provisions are made
by law for the Government to finance its immediate fiscal
requirements.
129.  (1) Notwithstanding the prohibition in subsection
(1) of section 87, any outstanding credit of the Central Bank
to  the  Government  as  at  the  appointed  date  may  be
maintained.
(2)    The  Central  Bank  shall,  in  consultation  with  the
Minister, convert any outstanding credit of the Central Bank
to the Government as at the appointed date, over a period of
ten years immediately succeeding such date, into negotiable
debt instruments with a specified maturity period issued at
prevailing market-related interest rates, on which the Central
Bank shall, as much as possible sell such debt instruments
under its monetary policy.
130.   Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (a) of
subsection (1) of section 115, any outstanding credit granted
to credit institutions pursuant to section 88a of the Monetary
Law Act (Chapter 422) and any credit guarantee given under
section  108  or  108a  of  the  said  Act  shall  be  maintained
under this Act subject to the terms and conditions as agreed.
